title: Company-wide policies and processes
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and commonly used internal templates. It is intended for all employees, contractors, and vendors who interact with company systems and data.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide a single reference for consistent, auditable, and operationally safe practices across the company.
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood systems, cloud accounts, on-premises resources, vendor engagements, and employee-initiated procurement or travel.
- Exceptions: Any exceptions require documented approval from the relevant domain owner and security sign-off; see the "Exceptions and Risk Acceptance" section.

Ownership and governance:
- Document owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.example.com).
- Security owner: Security & Compliance (security@redwood.example.com).
- Procurement owner: Finance (finance@redwood.example.com).
- Review cycle: Mandatory review every 12 months or after material changes to tooling, regulatory requirements, or business model.

1) Access & permissions:
Principles:
- Least privilege: Grant the minimum permissions required for a user or service to perform their job.
- Role-based access: Use RBAC groups tied to job functions (e.g., eng-infra-admins, sdr-sales, finance-approvers).
- Just-in-time and temporary access where feasible.
- Multi-factor authentication required for all accounts with access to production resources.

Onboarding:
- New hires: People Ops initiates account creation. Role templates (see Internal Templates) should be used to assign group memberships.
- Contractor access: Time-limited accounts with explicit end date; contractors must be sponsored by a full-time employee.

Offboarding:
1. People Ops triggers deprovisioning on termination date.
2. Managers confirm return of company assets.
3. Access removal checklist executed by eng-infra within 8 business hours for terminated employees and 24 hours for contractors.

Access request process:
- Self-service requests through the Access Portal (link: /tools/access-portal).
- Requests must include business justification, approver (manager), and duration if temporary.
- Access reviews: Quarterly audit of high-privilege groups (owners: Security & eng-infra).

Privileged access controls:
- MFA and SSO: Enforced via company SSO provider for all internal tools and cloud consoles.
- Break-glass process: Emergency access requires an approved ticket in the incident tracker and an audit log entry; access is time-boxed and reviewed post-event.

Key thresholds and SLOs:
- Access request turnaround: Standard requests ≤ 3 business days; urgent ≤ 8 hours.
- Offboarding access removal for terminated employees ≤ 8 business hours.

2) Change management:
Scope:
- Applies to changes that affect production, customer-facing systems, security controls, or billing.

Change types and process:
- Standard changes: Low-risk, repeatable, pre-approved (example: scheduled cert renewals).
- Minor changes: Non-production changes or changes that can be validated in staging. Requires owner approval and a review note.
- Major changes: Any change impacting production latency, availability, or data; requires Change Advisory Board (CAB) approval.

Change request procedure (high-level):
1. Submit a Change Request (CR) in the Change Tracker with description, rollback plan, test plan, and scheduled window.
2. Reviewer assignment: Automation routes CRs to owners and the CAB for major changes.
3. Approval: CAB votes on major changes at weekly meeting; emergency changes handled via expedited review.
4. Implementation: Follow the runbook and monitor defined metrics.
5. Post-change review: Document outcomes and update runbooks if needed.

Emergency changes:
- Emergency CAB: Convened ad-hoc; all emergency changes must be tracked and retroactively submitted to the Change Tracker within 24 hours.
- Rollback criteria must be defined in the CR.

Maintenance windows and communications:
- Scheduled maintenance windows: Saturdays 02:00–06:00 UTC for non-critical infra; customer-impacting windows require 72-hour notice.
- Customer communications: Product & Ops coordinate release notes and status-page messages.

3) Data management:
Data classification:
- Public: Information safe for public consumption.
- Internal: Non-sensitive internal information.
- Confidential: Customer data, PII, and business-sensitive info.
- Restricted: Regulated data (e.g., payment card data, health data) or data requiring contractual controls.

Handling rules by classification:
- Encryption: All Confidential and Restricted data must be encrypted at rest and in transit.
- Access: Confidential/Restricted data require explicit approval and logging.
- Storage: Avoid storing production customer data in development environments; if necessary, use sanitized or synthetic data and document the reason.

Retention and deletion:
- Default retention schedules: Logs = 90 days (short term) / 13 months (archived), Customer PII = per contract (default 7 years unless specified).
- Data deletion: Requests must follow the Data Deletion playbook (see related page).

Backups and disaster recovery:
- Backups: Daily incremental, weekly full backups for persistent stores that host customer data.
- Restore RTO targets: 4 hours for critical services, 24 hours for non-critical.
- Restore validation: Quarterly restore drills for critical datasets (owner: eng-sre).

Data transfers and third parties:
- Cross-border transfers require legal review for residency or compliance obligations.
- Vendors receiving Confidential/Restricted data must pass vendor security review and sign appropriate DPA.

Data incident reporting:
- All suspected data exposures must be reported immediately to security@redwood.example.com and filed as an Incident within 2 hours.
- Security will triage and follow incident response procedures; legal and communications will be looped in as required.

4) Procurement & expenses:
Approval matrix and thresholds:
- ≤ $1,000: Manager approval.
- $1,001–$25,000: Dept head approval + Finance notification.
- > $25,000: VP-level approval + Procurement involvement; some categories require CEO approval.

Preferred vendors and purchasing steps:
1. Check Preferred Vendor List (PVL) for existing agreements.
2. If PVL vendor available: submit PO request via Procurement portal.
3. If new vendor: complete vendor onboarding questionnaire and security review.
4. Finance issues PO and tracks spend against budget.

Expense reimbursements:
- Submit receipts within 30 days. Use the Expenses template for per-diem and non-travel expenses.
- Reimbursement timelines: standard payroll cycle; expedited reimburses rare (finance@redwood.example.com).

Purchase orders and invoicing:
- All vendor commitments > $5,000 must have a signed PO.
- Invoices should be sent to ap-invoices@redwood.example.com and must reference PO number.

Capital vs operating expense guidance:
- Capital purchases (hardware > $5,000) require finance tagging and asset registration.
- Small hardware purchases (< $5,000) may be expensed with manager approval.

5) Vendor management:
Onboarding checklist:
- Business justification and owner identified.
- Security questionnaire completed and reviewed by Security.
- Contract terms reviewed by Legal and Finance (SLAs, data residency, termination rights, liability).
- DPA executed if vendor will process customer data.

Ongoing vendor governance:
- Quarterly vendor health checks for critical vendors (ops availability, incident history, performance).
- Annual security attestation required for vendors with access to Confidential/Restricted data.
- Renewal: Begin commercial and security review 90 days before contract expiry.

Escalation and termination:
- Performance issues: Owner escalates to procurement and legal; remediation timeline defined in contract.
- Immediate termination: Finance/Legal may terminate for material security breaches or contract violations; transition plan required.

6) Travel policy:
Booking and approvals:
- All travel must be booked via the approved travel portal or agency.
- Domestic travel under $2,000: Manager approval. International or > $2,000: Dept head approval plus travel risk review for certain regions.

Allowances and expenses:
- Per diem: $75 domestic day, $125 international day (examples – use Expenses template for exact rules).
- Air travel: Economy for flights < 6 hours; business for flights ≥ 6 hours for senior roles as defined in the Travel Templates.
- Lodging: Mid-range hotels; exceptions require pre-approval.

Safety and duty of care:
- Notify People Ops of travel to high-risk regions; emergency contact info must be provided.
- Travel insurance and medical evacuation coverage procured for high-risk travel by People Ops.

COVID/health considerations:
- Follow CDC/WHO guidance and local entry rules. People Ops will update guidance as required.

7) Internal templates and runbooks:
Included templates (use these to standardize approvals and reduce audit friction):
- Role-based access templates (RBAC assignment CSV).
- Access Request form (Access Portal JSON).
- Change Request template (CR template).
- Procurement PO request template.
- Vendor onboarding checklist.
- Expense reimbursement form.
- Travel request and risk assessment template.
- Exception request and risk acceptance form.

How to use templates:
- Templates are stored in the company templates library: /confluence/templates and in the shared drive: /drive/company-templates.
- Always attach the filled template to the originating ticket (Access Portal, Change Tracker, Procurement portal).

Exceptions and risk acceptance:
- Submit an Exception Request using the template; must include business justification, compensating controls, expiration date, and risk owner.
- Security & domain owner must approve; high-risk exceptions require Legal sign-off.

Audit and compliance:
- This document and associated templates are part of Redwood’s internal control framework and are referenced in external audits.
- Keep artifacts (approval emails, tickets, signed contracts) for a minimum of 7 years unless otherwise specified.

Appendices:
A. Contact matrix:
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.example.com
- Security: security@redwood.example.com
- Procurement/Finance: procurement@redwood.example.com / finance@redwood.example.com
- IT & Eng Infra: eng-infra@redwood.example.com

B. Quick checklist (for managers):
- New hire: fill onboarding form, assign role template, sponsor contractor if needed.
- Access request: validate justification, set expiration for temporary access.
- Vendor: confirm security review and DPA before sharing Confidential data.
- Change: ensure CR has rollback plan and monitoring.
- Travel: verify approvals, risk review for international travel.

C. Revision history:
- 2024-11-01: Initial consolidation (Maya Chen).
- 2025-06-10: Added vendor security attestation process (reviewer: Priya Nair).
- 2026-03-01: Updated access review cadence and backup restore RTOs (Maya Chen).

Feedback and updates:
- To propose edits or request additional templates, file a doc update ticket at /confluence/requests or email people-ops@redwood.example.com.

End of document.
